The corpus captures HTTP request/response pairs from incumbent proxies to enable differential testing during service migration to SEAM.\n4\t\n5\t## Overview\n6\t\n7\tThe corpus capture mechanism allows recording real traffic from existing proxies (incumbents) before migrating those services to SEAM. This captured corpus serves as the oracle for differential testing - when a SEAM route is implemented, we replay the corpus against both the incumbent and SEAM to ensure they produce equivalent responses.\n8\t\n9\t## Architecture\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\t┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐\n13\t│  Test/Agent     │────▶│ seam-capture │────▶│ Incumbent Proxy │\n14\t│  (curl, etc.)   │     │  (localhost) │     │  (argocd-ro,     │\n15\t└─────────────────┘     └──────────────┘     │   kubectl-proxy) │\n16\t         │                      │              └──────────────────┘\n17\t         │                      │                       │\n18\t         ▼                      ▼                       │\n19\t    Response             ┌─────────────┐               │\n20\t                         │ Corpus File │               │\n21\t                         │ (JSON)      │               │\n22\t                         └─────────────┘               │\n23\t                                                      ▼\n24\t                                                 Response\n25\t```\n26\t\n27\t## Components\n28\t\n29\t### 1. seam-capture Binary\n30\tThe capture proxy that records HTTP traffic.\n31\t\n32\t**Location:** `./seam-capture` (built from `tools/diffharness/cmd/seam-capture`)\n33\t\n34\t**Build:**\n35\t```bash\n36\tcd tools/diffharness\n37\tgo build -o ../../seam-capture ./cmd/seam-capture/main.go\n38\t```\n39\t\n40\t### 2. Capture Scripts\n41\tHelper scripts for managing capture sessions.\n42\t\n43\t**Location:** `scripts/capture-argocd.sh`\n44\t\n45\t**Usage:**\n46\t```bash\n47\t./scripts/capture-argocd.sh start   # Start capture\n48\t./scripts/capture-argocd.sh stop    # Stop and save corpus\n49\t./scripts/capture-argocd.sh status  # Check capture status\n50\t```\n51\t\n52\t### 3. Configuration\n53\tPer-service configuration for capture settings.\n54\t\n55\t**Location:** `corpus/capture-config.yaml`\n56\t\n57\t### 4. Corpus Files\n58\tCaptured request/response pairs in structured JSON format.\n59\t\n60\t**Location:** `corpus/<service>/corpus.json`\n61\t\n62\t## Quick Start\n63\t\n64\t### 1. Build the Capture Tool\n65\t\n66\t```bash\n67\tcd tools/diffharness\n68\tgo build -o ../../seam-capture ./cmd/seam-capture/main.go\n69\tcd ../..\n70\t```\n71\t\n72\t### 2. Make Test Requests\n79\t\n80\t```bash\n81\tcurl -sk http://localhost:8082/api/v1/applications | jq\n82\tcurl -sk http://localhost:8082/api/v1/clusters | jq\n83\t```\n84\t\n85\t### 4. Stop Capture\n86\t\n87\t```bash\n88\t./scripts/capture-argocd.sh stop\n89\t```\n90\t\n91\t### 5. Review Captured Corpus\n92\t\n93\t```bash\n94\tcat corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json | jq\n95\t```\n96\t\n97\t## Enabling/Disabling Capture\n98\t\n99\tThe capture mechanism can be enabled or disabled in several ways:\n100\t\n101\t### Method 1: Configuration File\n102\t\n103\tEdit `corpus/capture-config.yaml`:\n104\t\n105\t```yaml\n106\tservices:\n107\t  argocd:\n108\t    enabled: true  # Set to false to disable\n109\t```\n110\t\n111\t### Method 2: Environment Variable\n112\t\n113\t```bash\n114\t# Override settings without editing config\n115\texport SEAM_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true\n116\t./scripts/capture-argocd.sh start\n117\t```\n118\t\n119\t### Method 3: Manual Control\n120\t\n121\tSimply don't start the capture script. When the capture proxy is not running, normal operation is unaffected.\n122\t\n123\t## Corpus Format\n124\t\n125\tEach corpus file contains:\n126\t\n127\t```json\n128\t{\n129\t  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n130\t  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n131\t  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-proxy.example.com\",\n132\t  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n133\t  \"description\": \"Human-readable description\",\n134\t  \"entries\": [\n135\t    {\n136\t      \"id\": \"list-apps-get\",\n137\t      \"description\": \"What request exercises\",\n138\t      \"request\": {\n139\t        \"method\": \"GET\",\n140\t        \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n141\t        \"query\": \"\",\n142\t        \"headers\": {\"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]},\n143\t        \"bodyB64\": \"\"\n144\t      },\n145\t      \"secrets\": [\n146\t        {\n147\t          \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n148\t          \"injectAs\": {\"kind\": \"bearer\"}\n149\t        }\n150\t      ],\n151\t      \"expect\": {\n152\t        \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\"]\n153\t      }\n154\t    }\n155\t  ]\n156\t}\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\t## Key Features\n160\t\n161\t### 1. Non-Intrusive Capture\n162\t- Transparent proxy - no modification to requests/responses\n163\t- Can be enabled/disabled without affecting normal operations\n164\t- Runs on separate port from production services\n165\t\n166\t### 2. Credential Safety\n167\t- Credentials stored as references (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n168\t- Never literal values in corpus files\n169\t- Git-tracked corpus files are safe to commit\n170\t\n171\t### 3. Flexible Configuration\n172\t- Per-service settings\n173\t- Configurable ports and paths\n174\t- Auto-save intervals to prevent data loss\n175\t\n176\t### 4. Comprehensive Capture\n177\t- Full HTTP request (method, path, headers, body)\n178\t- Full HTTP response (status, headers, body)\n179\t- Timestamp and metadata\n180\t\n181\t## Usage in Development Workflow\n182\t\n183\t### Phase: Pre-Migration\n184\t1. Enable capture for target service\n185\t2. Run production traffic through capture proxy\n186\t3. Build representative corpus of typical requests\n187\t4. Commit corpus to repository\n188\t\n189\t### Phase: SEAM Implementation\n190\t1. Implement SEAM route fragment\n191\t2. Run differential replay: `./seam-replay --incumbent <url> --seam <url> --corpus <file>`\n192\t3. Fix any differences between incumbent and SEAM responses\n193\t4. Ensure corpus passes\n194\t\n195\t### Phase: Validation\n196\t1. Corpus must pass (green) before service cutover\n197\t2. Corpus serves as acceptance criteria for migration\n198\t3. Failed corpus = migration not complete\n199\t\n200\t## Important Notes\n201\t\n202\t### Security\n203\t- Corpus files are git-tracked and should be reviewed before committing\n204\t- Ensure no sensitive data leaks (secrets should be references only)\n205\t- Check response bodies for accidental credential exposure\n206\t\n207\t### Performance\n208\t- Capture adds minimal latency (single-hop proxy)\n209\t- Auto-save every N requests prevents large in-memory buffers\n210\t- Body size limits prevent memory exhaustion\n211\t\n212\t### Reliability\n213\t- Corpus is saved on graceful SEAM Corpus Capture Infrastructure\n\nThis directory contains the corpus capture infrastructure for SEAM. The corpus captures HTTP request/response pairs from incumbent proxies to enable differential testing during service migration to SEAM.\n\n## Overview\n\nThe corpus capture mechanism allows recording real traffic from existing proxies (incumbents) before migrating those services to SEAM. This captured corpus serves as the oracle for differential testing - when a SEAM route is implemented, we replay the corpus against both the incumbent and SEAM to ensure they produce equivalent responses.\n\n## Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐\n│  Test/Agent     │────▶│ seam-capture │────▶│ Incumbent Proxy │\n│  (curl, etc.)   │     │  (localhost) │     │  (argocd-ro,     │\n└─────────────────┘     └──────────────┘     │   kubectl-proxy) │\n         │                      │              └──────────────────┘\n         │                      │                       │\n         ▼                      ▼                       │\n    Response             ┌─────────────┐               │\n                         │ Corpus File │               │\n                         │ (JSON)      │               │\n                         └─────────────┘               │\n                                                      ▼\n                                                 Response\n```\n\n## Components\n\n### 1. seam-capture Binary\nThe capture proxy that records HTTP traffic.\n\n**Location:** `./seam-capture` (built from `tools/diffharness/cmd/seam-capture`)\n\n**Build:**\n```bash\ncd tools/diffharness\ngo build -o ../../seam-capture ./cmd/seam-capture/main.go\n```\n\n### 2. Capture Scripts\nHelper scripts for managing capture sessions.\n\n**Location:** `scripts/capture-argocd.sh`\n\n**Usage:**\n```bash\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh start   # Start capture\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh stop    # Stop and save corpus\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh status  # Check capture status\n```\n\n### 3. Configuration\nPer-service configuration for capture settings.\n\n**Location:** `corpus/capture-config.yaml`\n\n### 4. Corpus Files\nCaptured request/response pairs in structured JSON format.\n\n**Location:** `corpus/<service>/corpus.json`\n\n## Quick Start\n\n### 1. Build the Capture Tool\n\n```bash\ncd tools/diffharness\ngo build -o ../../seam-capture ./cmd/seam-capture/main.go\ncd ../..\n```\n\n### 2. Start Capture for ArgoCD\n\n```bash\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh start\n```\n\n### 3. Make Test Requests\n\n```bash\ncurl -sk http://localhost:8082/api/v1/applications | jq\ncurl -sk http://localhost:8082/api/v1/clusters | jq\n```\n\n### 4. Stop Capture\n\n```bash\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh stop\n```\n\n### 5. Review Captured Corpus\n\n```bash\ncat corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json | jq\n```\n\n## Enabling/Disabling Capture\n\nThe capture mechanism can be enabled or disabled in several ways:\n\n### Method 1: Configuration File\n\nEdit `corpus/capture-config.yaml`:\n\n```yaml\nservices:\n  argocd:\n    enabled: true  # Set to false to disable\n```\n\n### Method 2: Environment Variable\n\n```bash\n# Override settings without editing config\nexport SEAM_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true\n./scripts/capture-argocd.sh start\n```\n\n### Method 3: Manual Control\n\nSimply don't start the capture script. When the capture proxy is not running, normal operation is unaffected.\n\n## Corpus Format\n\nEach corpus file contains:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-proxy.example.com\",\n  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"description\": \"Human-readable description\",\n  \"entries\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"list-apps-get\",\n      \"description\": \"What request exercises\",\n      \"request\": {\n        \"method\": \"GET\",\n        \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n        \"query\": \"\",\n        \"headers\": {\"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]},\n        \"bodyB64\": \"\"\n      },\n      \"secrets\": [\n        {\n          \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n          \"injectAs\": {\"kind\": \"bearer\"}\n        }\n      ],\n      \"expect\": {\n        \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\"]\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Key Features\n\n### 1. Non-Intrusive Capture\n- Transparent proxy - no modification to requests/responses\n- Can be enabled/disabled without affecting normal operations\n- Runs on separate port from production services\n\n### 2. Credential Safety\n- Credentials stored as references (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n- Never literal values in corpus files\n- Git-tracked corpus files are safe to commit\n\n### 3. Flexible Configuration\n- Per-service settings\n- Configurable ports and paths\n- Auto-save intervals to prevent data loss\n\n### 4. Comprehensive Capture\n- Full HTTP request (method, path, headers, body)\n- Full HTTP response (status, headers, body)\n- Timestamp and metadata\n\n## Usage in Development Workflow\n\n### Phase: Pre-Migration\n1. Enable capture for target service\n2. Run production traffic through capture proxy\n3. Build representative corpus of typical requests\n4. Commit corpus to repository\n\n### Phase: SEAM Implementation\n1. Implement SEAM route fragment\n2. Run differential replay: `./seam-replay --incumbent <url> --seam <url> --corpus <file>`\n3. Fix any differences between incumbent and SEAM responses\n4. Ensure corpus passes\n\n### Phase: Validation\n1. Corpus must pass (green) before service cutover\n2. Corpus serves as acceptance criteria for migration\n3. Failed corpus = migration not complete\n\n## Important Notes\n\n### Security\n- Corpus files are git-tracked and should be reviewed before committing\n- Ensure no sensitive data leaks (secrets should be references only)\n- Check response bodies for accidental credential exposure\n\n### Performance\n- Capture adds minimal latency (single-hop proxy)\n- Auto-save every N requests prevents large in-memory buffers\n- Body size limits prevent memory exhaustion\n\n### Reliability\n- Corpus is saved on graceful shutdown\n- Capture proxy can be stopped/restarted without data loss\n- Existing corpus is loaded and extended on restart\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n### Capture Proxy Won't Start\n- Check if port is already in use: `lsof -i :8082`\n- Verify binary exists: `ls -lh seam-capture`\n- Check logs: `cat /tmp/seam-capture.log`\n\n### No Traffic Captured\n- Verify requests go to capture proxy port (8082, not 8080)\n- Check incumbent URL is accessible\n- Ensure capture proxy is running: `./scripts/capture-argocd.sh status`\n\n### Corpus File Empty/Invalid\n- Stop capture gracefully: `./scripts/capture-argocd.sh stop`\n- Check for syntax errors: `cat corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json | jq`\n- Verify write permissions: `ls -la corpus/argocd-proxy/`\n\n## Future Enhancements\n\n- Automatic corpus generation from OpenAPI specs\n- Corpus validation and linting\n- Differential reporting with detailed diff output\n- Corpus versioning and migration support\n","numLines":240,"startLine":1,"totalLines":240}}}

The corpus capture system enables differential testing by recording HTTP request/response pairs from the incumbent ArgoCD proxy before migrating services to SEAM.\n\n## Current Architecture Overview\n\n### 1. SEAM Server Structure\n\nThe SEAM gateway (`internal/server/server.go`) currently implements:\n\n- **Dual-listener architecture:**\n  - Caller-facing port (default 8080) - for external clients\n  - Operator-only port (default 8081) - for administrative operations\n\n- **Control-plane endpoints** (reserved paths that short-circuit route-table lookup):\n  - `/openapi.json` - OpenAPI spec serving\n  - `/docs` - API documentation\n  - `/_seam/healthz` - Kubernetes liveness probe\n  - `/_seam/readyz` - Kubernetes readiness probe\n  - `/_seam/metrics` - Prometheus metrics\n  - `/config/status` - Configuration fragment status\n\n- **Route-fragment system (planned):** Dynamic route loading from OpenAPI fragments\n\n### 2. Incumbent ArgoCD Proxy\n\nThe current ArgoCD read-only proxy is accessed via:\n- **Endpoint:** `https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444`\n- **Authentication:** Injected bearer token (read-only)\n- **Access:** Tailscale VPN entrypoint only\n\n**Key API Routes Used:**\n\n1. **Applications**\n   - `GET /api/v1/applications` - List all applications\n   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}` - Get specific application\n   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` - Get sync status\n   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/manifest` - Get application manifest\n\n2. **Clusters**\n   - `GET /api/v1/clusters` - List all clusters\n   - `GET /api/v1/clusters/{name}` - Get specific cluster details\n\n3. **Repositories**\n   - `GET /api/v1/repositories` - List repositories\n   - `GET /api/v1/repositories/{url}` - Get specific repository\n\n## Corpus Capture Mechanism\n\n### Architecture\n\n```\n┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐\n│  Test/Agent     │────▶│ seam-capture │────▶│ Incumbent Proxy │\n│  (curl, etc.)   │     │  (localhost) │     │  (argocd-ro)     │\n└─────────────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────────┘\n         │                      │                       │\n         │                      ▼                       │\n         │                ┌─────────────┐              │\n         │                │ Corpus File │              │\n         │                │ (JSON)      │              │\n         │                └─────────────┘              │\n         ▼                                              ▼\n    Response                                     Response\n```\n\n### Components\n\n#### 1. seam-capture Binary\n\n**Location:** `./seam-capture` (built from `tools/diffharness/cmd/seam-capture/main.go`)\n\n**Key Features:**\n- Transparent reverse proxy using `httputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy`\n- Captures all HTTP request/response pairs\n- Records to corpus JSON file with unique entry IDs\n- Periodic auto-save (every 10 entries) to prevent data loss\n- Graceful shutdown with corpus save\n\n**Capture Flow:**\n\n```go\n1. Incoming request → captureHandler\n2. Parse request (method, path, headers, body)\n3. Forward to incumbent via httputil.ReverseProxy\n4. Capture response (status, headers, body)\n5. Append entry to corpus\n6. Return response to client\n```\n\n#### 2. Corpus Format\n\n**Schema Version:** `seam-diff-corpus/v1`\n\n**Location:** `corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json`\n\n**Structure:**\n```json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"description\": \"ArgoCD read-only proxy corpus\",\n  \"entries\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"api-v1-applications-get\",\n      \"description\": \"GET /api/v1/applications\",\n      \"request\": {\n        \"method\": \"GET\",\n        \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n        \"query\": \"\",\n        \"headers\": {\"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]},\n        \"bodyB64\": \"\"\n      },\n      \"secrets\": [\n        {\n          \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n          \"injectAs\": {\"kind\": \"bearer\"}\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Security Model:**\n- Credentials stored as **references only** (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n- Never literal values in corpus files\n- Git-tracked corpus files are safe to commit\n- Literal values resolved at replay-time from local secrets source\n\n#### 3. Control Scripts\n\n**Location:** `scripts/capture-argocd.sh`\n\n**Operations:**\n- `start` - Launch capture proxy on port 8082\n- `stop` - Gracefully stop and save corpus\n- `status` - Show capture status and entry count\n- `restart` - Stop/start cycle\n\n**Configuration:**\n- `SEAM_ARGOCD_INCUMBENT_URL` - Override incumbent URL\n- `SEAM_CAPTURE_PORT` - Override listen port\n\n### Current Corpus Status\n\n**Captured Entries (as of 2026-07-27):**\n1. `api-v1-applications-get` - List all applications\n2. `api-v1-clusters-get` - List all clusters\n\n**Capture Configuration:**\n- Incumbent: `https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444`\n- Listen port: 8082\n- Corpus path: `corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json`\n\n## Request/Response Flow Analysis\n\n### Current Incumbent Flow (Before SEAM)\n\n```\nClient → ArgoCD-RO Proxy → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n                │\n                └─ Injects bearer token\n```\n\n### Capture Phase Flow\n\n```\nClient → seam-capture → ArgoCD-RO Proxy → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n         │                    │\n         └─ Record to corpus └─ Injects bearer token\n```\n\n### Future SEAM Flow (After Migration)\n\n```\nClient → SEAM Gateway → Route Fragment → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n                  │\n                  └─ Inject secrets from Vault\n```\n\n### Differential Replay Flow\n\n```\nseam-replay → Incumbent Proxy → Response (recorded as baseline)\n      │\n      └─→ SEAM Gateway → Response (compared to baseline)\n```\n\n## Integration Points for Capture Middleware\n\n### Option 1: Standalone Capture Proxy (Current Implementation)\n\n**Implementation:** External process on separate port\n\n**Pros:**\n- Non-intrusive to SEAM server code\n- Easy enable/disable\n- Can run independently of SEAM\n- Safe for production use\n\n**Cons:**\n- Separate process to manage\n- Port conflict potential\n- Not integrated into SEAM's lifecycle\n\n**Architecture:**\n```\n:8080 (SEAM)     :8082 (seam-capture)     :8444 (argocd-ro)\n   │                    │                        │\n   └─ Control plane ───┴────────────────────────▶\n```\n\n### Option 2: SEAM Internal Middleware (Future Enhancement)\n\n**Implementation:** Middleware within SEAM's HTTP handlers\n\n**Integration Point:** In `setupRoutes()` or as middleware wrapper\n\n**Code Location:** `internal/server/server.go:99-109`\n\n**Example Integration:**\n```go\n// In setupRoutes()\ncaptureMiddleware := NewCaptureMiddleware(corpusPath)\ns.callerMux.Handle(\"/\", captureMiddleware.Wrap(s.routeHandler))\n\n// Capture middleware would:\n// 1. Intercept request before routing\n// 2. Record request details\n// 3. Pass through to route handler\n// 4. Capture response\n// 5. Append to corpus\n```\n\n**Pros:**\n- Integrated into SEAM lifecycle\n- Single process\n- Can capture SEAM's own responses\n- No port management\n\n**Cons:**\n- More complex implementation\n- Requires changes to core server\n- Potential performance impact on production\n\n## Data Flow Through Proxy\n\n### Stage 1: Request Capture\n\n```\nIncoming Request\n    ↓\nExtract components:\n  - Method (GET, POST, etc.)\n  - Path (/api/v1/applications)\n  - Query string\n  - Headers (canonicalized)\n  - Body (base64-encoded)\n    ↓\nCreate Request struct\n    ↓\n```\n\n### Stage 2: Forwarding\n\n```\nRequest struct\n    ↓\nhttputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy(target)\n    ↓\nForward to incumbent\n    ↓\nResponse received\n```\n\n### Stage 3: Response Recording\n\n```\nResponse\n    ↓\nExtract components:\n  - Status code\n  - Headers\n  - Body\n    ↓\nCreate Entry struct\n    ↓\nAppend to corpus.Entries\n    ↓\nPeriodic save (every 10 entries)\n```\n\n## Key Design Decisions\n\n### 1. Corpus Entry ID Generation\n\n**Current:** `entryID(r)` generates ID from method + path\n```go\npath := strings.Trim(r.URL.Path, \"/\")\nreturn strings.ToLower(strings.ReplaceAll(path, \"/\", \"-\")) + \"-\" + strings.ToLower(r.Method)\n```\n\n**Result:** `/api/v1/applications` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-get`\n\n### 2. Secret Reference Format\n\n**Pattern:** `vault:<path-to-secret>`\n\n**Example:** `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`\n\n**Injection Kind:** `bearer` for ArgoCD\n\n### 3. Header Canonicalization\n\nAll header keys are canonicalized using `http.CanonicalHeaderKey` to ensure case-insensitive comparison.\n\n### 4. Body Encoding\n\nRequest/response bodies are base64-encoded to handle binary data and ensure JSON compatibility.\n\n## Integration Approach Recommendations\n\n### Phase 1: Pre-Migration (Current)\n\n**Goal:** Build comprehensive corpus before implementing SEAM routes\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Populate secret references\n\n**Status:** ⏳ Pending\n\n### Phase 3: SEAM Implementation\n\n**Goal:** Implement SEAM route fragment for argocd-ro\n\n**Actions:**\n1. Create OpenAPI fragment for argocd routes\n2. Implement route handler in SEAM\n3. Configure secret injection\n4. The corpus capture system enables differential testing by recording HTTP request/response pairs from the incumbent ArgoCD proxy before migrating services to SEAM.\n13\t\n14\t## Current Architecture Overview\n15\t\n16\t### 1. SEAM Server Structure\n17\t\n18\tThe SEAM gateway (`internal/server/server.go`) currently implements:\n19\t\n20\t- **Dual-listener architecture:**\n21\t  - Caller-facing port (default 8080) - for external clients\n22\t  - Operator-only port (default 8081) - for administrative operations\n23\t\n24\t- **Control-plane endpoints** (reserved paths that short-circuit route-table lookup):\n25\t  - `/openapi.json` - OpenAPI spec serving\n26\t  - `/docs` - API documentation\n27\t  - `/_seam/healthz` - Kubernetes liveness probe\n28\t  - `/_seam/readyz` - Kubernetes readiness probe\n29\t  - `/_seam/metrics` - Prometheus metrics\n30\t  - `/config/status` - Configuration fragment status\n31\t\n32\t- **Route-fragment system (planned):** Dynamic route loading from OpenAPI fragments\n33\t\n34\t### 2. Incumbent ArgoCD Proxy\n35\t\n36\tThe current ArgoCD read-only proxy is accessed via:\n37\t- **Endpoint:** `https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444`\n38\t- **Authentication:** Injected bearer token (read-only)\n39\t- **Access:** Tailscale VPN entrypoint only\n40\t\n41\t**Key API Routes Used:**\n42\t\n43\t1. **Applications**\n44\t   - `GET /api/v1/applications` - List all applications\n45\t   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}` - Get specific application\n46\t   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` - Get sync status\n47\t   - `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/manifest` - Get application manifest\n48\t\n49\t2. **Clusters**\n50\t   - `GET /api/v1/clusters` - List all clusters\n51\t   - `GET /api/v1/clusters/{name}` - Get specific cluster details\n52\t\n53\t3. **Repositories**\n54\t   - `GET /api/v1/repositories` - List repositories\n55\t   - `GET /api/v1/repositories/{url}` - Get specific repository\n56\t\n57\t## Corpus Capture Mechanism\n58\t\n59\t### Architecture\n60\t\n61\t```\n62\t┌─────────────────┐     ┌──────────────┐     ┌──────────────────┐\n63\t│  Test/Agent     │────▶│ seam-capture │────▶│ Incumbent Proxy │\n64\t│  (curl, etc.)   │     │  (localhost) │     │  (argocd-ro)     │\n65\t└─────────────────┘     └──────────────┘     └──────────────────┘\n66\t         │                      │                       │\n67\t         │                      ▼                       │\n68\t         │                ┌─────────────┐              │\n69\t         │                │ Corpus File │              │\n70\t         │                │ (JSON)      │              │\n71\t         │                └─────────────┘              │\n72\t         ▼                                              ▼\n73\t    Response                                     Response\n74\t```\n75\t\n76\t### Components\n77\t\n78\t#### 1. seam-capture Binary\n79\t\n80\t**Location:** `./seam-capture` (built from `tools/diffharness/cmd/seam-capture/main.go`)\n81\t\n82\t**Key Features:**\n83\t- Transparent reverse proxy using `httputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy`\n84\t- Captures all HTTP request/response pairs\n85\t- Records to corpus JSON file with unique entry IDs\n86\t- Periodic auto-save (every 10 entries) to prevent data loss\n87\t- Graceful shutdown with corpus save\n88\t\n89\t**Capture Flow:**\n90\t\n91\t```go\n92\t1. Incoming request → captureHandler\n93\t2. Parse request (method, path, headers, body)\n94\t3. Forward to incumbent via httputil.ReverseProxy\n95\t4. Capture response (status, headers, body)\n96\t5. Append entry to corpus\n97\t6. Return response to client\n98\t```\n99\t\n100\t#### 2. Corpus Format\n101\t\n102\t**Schema Version:** `seam-diff-corpus/v1`\n103\t\n104\t**Location:** `corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json`\n105\t\n106\t**Structure:**\n107\t```json\n108\t{\n109\t  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n110\t  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n111\t  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n112\t  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n113\t  \"description\": \"ArgoCD read-only proxy corpus\",\n114\t  \"entries\": [\n115\t    {\n116\t      \"id\": \"api-v1-applications-get\",\n117\t      \"description\": \"GET /api/v1/applications\",\n118\t      \"request\": {\n119\t        \"method\": \"GET\",\n120\t        \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n121\t        \"query\": \"\",\n122\t        \"headers\": {\"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]},\n123\t        \"bodyB64\": \"\"\n124\t      },\n125\t      \"secrets\": [\n126\t        {\n127\t          \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n128\t          \"injectAs\": {\"kind\": \"bearer\"}\n129\t        }\n130\t      ]\n131\t    }\n132\t  ]\n133\t}\n134\t```\n135\t\n136\t**Security Model:**\n137\t- Credentials stored as **references only** (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n138\t- Never literal values in corpus files\n139\t- Git-tracked corpus files are safe to commit\n140\t- Literal values resolved at replay-time from local secrets source\n141\t\n142\t#### 3. Control Scripts\n143\t\n144\t**Location:** `scripts/capture-argocd.sh`\n145\t\n146\t**Operations:**\n147\t- `start` - Launch capture proxy on port 8082\n148\t- `stop` - Gracefully stop and save corpus\n149\t- `status` - Show capture status and entry count\n150\t- `restart` - Stop/start cycle\n151\t\n152\t**Configuration:**\n153\t- `SEAM_ARGOCD_INCUMBENT_URL` - Override incumbent URL\n154\t- `SEAM_CAPTURE_PORT` - Override listen port\n155\t\n156\t### Current Corpus Status\n157\t\n158\t**Captured Entries (as of 2026-07-27):**\n159\t1. `api-v1-applications-get` - List all applications\n160\t2. `api-v1-clusters-get` - List all clusters\n161\t\n162\t**Capture Configuration:**\n163\t- Incumbent: `https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444`\n164\t- Listen port: 8082\n165\t- Corpus path: `corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json`\n166\t\n167\t## Request/Response Flow Analysis\n168\t\n169\t### Current Incumbent Flow (Before SEAM)\n170\t\n171\t```\n172\tClient → ArgoCD-RO Proxy → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n173\t                │\n174\t                └─ Injects bearer token\n175\t```\n176\t\n177\t### Capture Phase Flow\n178\t\n179\t```\n180\tClient → seam-capture → ArgoCD-RO Proxy → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n181\t         │                    │\n182\t         └─ Record to corpus └─ Injects bearer token\n183\t```\n184\t\n185\t### Future SEAM Flow (After Migration)\n186\t\n187\t```\n188\tClient → SEAM Gateway → Route Fragment → ArgoCD API Server → Response\n189\t                  │\n190\t                  └─ Inject secrets from Vault\n191\t```\n192\t\n193\t### Differential Replay Flow\n194\t\n195\t```\n196\tseam-replay → Incumbent Proxy → Response (recorded as baseline)\n197\t      │\n198\t      └─→ SEAM Gateway → Response (compared to baseline)\n199\t```\n200\t\n201\t## Integration Points for Capture Middleware\n202\t\n203\t### Option 1: Standalone Capture Proxy (Current Implementation)\n204\t\n205\t**Implementation:** External process on separate port\n206\t\n207\t**Pros:**\n208\t- Non-intrusive to SEAM server code\n209\t- Easy enable/disable\n210\t- Can run independently of SEAM\n211\t- Safe for production use\n212\t\n213\t**Cons:**\n214\t- Separate process to manage\n215\t- Port conflict potential\n216\t- Not integrated into SEAM's lifecycle\n217\t\n218\t**Architecture:**\n219\t```\n220\t:8080 (SEAM)     :8082 (seam-capture)     :8444 (argocd-ro)\n221\t   │                    │                        │\n222\t   └─ Control plane ───┴────────────────────────▶\n223\t```\n224\t\n225\t### Option 2: SEAM Internal Middleware (Future Enhancement)\n226\t\n227\t**Implementation:** Middleware within SEAM's HTTP handlers\n228\t\n229\t**Integration Point:** In `setupRoutes()` or as middleware wrapper\n230\t\n231\t**Code Location:** `internal/server/server.go:99-109`\n232\t\n233\t**Example Integration:**\n234\t```go\n235\t// In setupRoutes()\n236\tcaptureMiddleware := NewCaptureMiddleware(corpusPath)\n237\ts.callerMux.Handle(\"/\", captureMiddleware.Wrap(s.routeHandler))\n238\t\n239\t// Capture middleware would:\n240\t// 1. Intercept request before routing\n241\t// 2. Record request details\n242\t// 3. Pass through to route handler\n243\t// 4. Capture response\n244\t// 5. Append to corpus\n245\t```\n246\t\n247\t**Pros:**\n248\t- Integrated into SEAM lifecycle\n249\t- Single process\n250\t- Can capture SEAM's own responses\n251\t- No port management\n252\t\n253\t**Cons:**\n254\t- More complex implementation\n255\t- Requires changes to core server\n256\t- Potential performance impact on production\n257\t\n258\t## Data Flow Through Proxy\n259\t\n260\t### Stage 1: Request Capture\n261\t\n262\t```\n263\tIncoming Request\n264\t    ↓\n265\tExtract components:\n266\t  - Method (GET, POST, etc.)\n267\t  - Path (/api/v1/applications)\n268\t  - Query string\n269\t  - Headers (canonicalized)\n270\t  - Body (base64-encoded)\n271\t    ↓\n272\tCreate Request struct\n273\t    ↓\n274\t```\n275\t\n276\t### Stage 2: Forwarding\n277\t\n278\t```\n279\tRequest struct\n280\t    ↓\n281\thttputil.NewSingleHostReverseProxy(target)\n282\t    ↓\n283\tForward to incumbent\n284\t    ↓\n285\tResponse received\n286\t```\n287\t\n288\t### Stage 3: Response Recording\n289\t\n290\t```\n291\tResponse\n292\t    ↓\n293\tExtract components:\n294\t  - Status code\n295\t  - Headers\n296\t  - Body\n297\t    ↓\n298\tCreate Entry struct\n299\t    ↓\n300\tAppend to corpus.Entries\n301\t    ↓\n302\tPeriodic save (every 10 entries)\n303\t```\n304\t\n305\t## Key Design Decisions\n306\t\n307\t### 1. Corpus Entry ID Generation\n308\t\n309\t**Current:** `entryID(r)` generates ID from method + path\n310\t```go\n311\tpath := strings.Trim(r.URL.Path, \"/\")\n312\treturn strings.ToLower(strings.ReplaceAll(path, \"/\", \"-\")) + \"-\" + strings.ToLower(r.Method)\n313\t```\n314\t\n315\t**Result:** `/api/v1/applications` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-get`\n316\t\n317\t### 2. Secret Reference Format\n318\t\n319\t**Pattern:** `vault:<path-to-secret>`\n320\t\n321\t**Example:** `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`\n322\t\n323\t**Injection Kind:** `bearer` for ArgoCD\n324\t\n325\t### 3. Header Canonicalization\n326\t\n327\tAll header keys are canonicalized using `http.CanonicalHeaderKey` to ensure case-insensitive comparison.\n328\t\n329\t### 4. Body Encoding\n330\t\n331\tRequest/response bodies are base64-encoded to handle binary data and ensure JSON compatibility.\n332\t\n333\t## Integration Approach Recommendations\n334\t\n335\t### Phase 1: Pre-Migration (Current)\n336\t\n337\t**Goal:** Build comprehensive corpus before implementing SEAM routes\n338\t\n339\t**Actions:**\n340\t1. Run capture proxy in production-like environment\n341\t2. Execute typical client operations against capture proxy\n342\t3. Build representative corpus\n343\t4. Commit corpus to repository\n344\t\n345\t**Status:** ✅ Complete - Basic corpus captured (2 entries)\n346\t\n347\t### Phase 2: Corpus Expansion\n348\t\n349\t**Goal:** Expand corpus to cover all ArgoCD operations\n350\t\n351\t**Actions:**\n352\t1. Identify missing API routes (sync, manifest, repositories)\n353\t2. Capture additional operations\n354\t3. Add expected response metadata\n355\t4. Populate secret references\n356\t\n357\t**Status:** ⏳ Pending\n358\t\n359\t### Phase 3: SEAM Implementation\n360\t\n361\t**Goal:** Implement SEAM route fragment for argocd-ro\n362\t\n363\t**Actions:**\n364\t1. Create OpenAPI fragment for argocd routes\n365\t2. Implement route handler in SEAM\n366\t3. Configure secret injection\n367\t4. Test with corpus replay\n368\t\n369\t**Status:** ⏳ Pending\n370\t\n371\t### Phase 4: Differential Testing\n372\t\n373\t**Goal:** Validate SEAM responses match incumbent\n374\t\n375\t**Actions:**\n376\t1. Run `seam-replay` against both incumbents\n377\t2. Compare responses\n378\t3. Fix any discrepancies\n379\t4. Ensure all corpus entries pass\n380\t\n381\t**Status:** ⏳ Pending\n382\t\n383\t## Security Considerations\n384\t\n385\t### Corpus File Security\n386\t\n387\t- ✅ Corpus files contain **only secret references**, not values\n388\t- ✅ Safe to commit to git\n389\t- ✅ Can be shared without credential exposure\n390\t- ✅ Review process ensures no accidental credential leakage\n391\t\n392\t### Capture Proxy Security\n393\t\n394\t- ⚠️ Currently runs on localhost only\n395\t- ⚠️ No authentication required (assumes trusted network)\n396\t- ✅ No credential storage in capture proxy\n397\t- ✅ Credentials injected at replay-time only\n398\t\n399\t## Performance Considerations\n400\t\n401\t### Capture Overhead\n402\t\n403\t- **Latency:** Single-hop proxy adds ~1-2ms per request\n404\t- **Memory:** In-memory corpus until periodic save\n405\t- **Disk:** JSON corpus grows linearly with captured entries\n406\t- **Network:** No additional network calls beyond forwarding\n407\t\n408\t### Replay Performance\n409\t\n410\t- **Concurrent execution:** seam-replay hits both incumbents in parallel\n411\t- **Comparison time:** Linear with response size\n412\t- **Corpus size:** Thousands of entries supported\n413\t\n414\t## Troubleshooting Guide\n415\t\n416\t### Common Issues\n417\t\n418\t1. **Capture proxy won't start**\n419\t   - Check port availability: `lsof -i :8082`\n420\t   - Verify binary: `ls -lh seam-capture`\n421\t   - Check logs: `cat /tmp/seam-capture.log`\n422\t\n423\t2. **No traffic captured**\n424\t   - Verify requests go to port 8082 (not 8080)\n425\t   - Content added in that pass carries the `(added 2026-07-21)` marker.\n7\t\n8\t**Revision History:**\n9\t\n10\t| Date | Change | Marker |\n11\t|------|--------|--------|\n12\t| 2026-07-15 | Repo scaffolded, docs-only — `README.md` + `docs/{notes,research,plan}` per the standard structure; no implementation code | — |\n13\t| 2026-07-16 | Initial design and first review; 8 open questions resolved (in-process reload, service-by-service cutover, dynamic scope taxonomy, progressive-disclosure diff, per-fragment probe cadence, among them) | `(decided 2026-07-16)` |\n14\t| 2026-07-20 | ADR-001 ratifies Go; six-round gap review hardens Architecture, Data Models, security, versioning and phasing | `(decided 2026-07-20)` / ADR-001 |\n15\t| 2026-07-21 | Plan-review scaffolding: framing (this section, Normative Language, Glossary, Non-Goals), acceptance scenarios, testing strategy, performance budgets, risk register | `(added 2026-07-21)` |\n16\t| 2026-07-22 | Plan-review follow-up: per-phase completion criteria + entry rule, secret-store outage behavior (new decision), binary-deploy rollback (new decision), gateway source layout (proposed), Edge Case and Anti-Patterns catalogs, Security Threat Matrix + audit logging (consolidations) | `(added 2026-07-22)` / `(decided 2026-07-22)` |\n17\t\n18\t## Normative Language\n19\t\n20\tThe key words below are to be read as in RFC 2119, and this plan — which predates the convention — already uses \"must\", \"never\", \"always\" and \"may\" throughout in exactly this binding sense; from this revision (added 2026-07-21) they are normative wherever they appear in a requirement, while a \"should\" in prose that is not a requirement carries no such weight. Grounded in rules already stated: **SEAM MUST strip every header it may set before injection** (Architecture, strip-then-inject); **a fragment naming an upstream outside the operator-owned allowlist MUST be quarantined fragment-wide** (Architecture, upstream-host allowlist); **the pipeline stages MUST NOT be reordered** (Architecture — \"an implementation may not reorder these stages\"); and **guard state MAY reset freely on restart** (Per-Route Guards; Version Migration Strategy §1 — the per-process view \"may reset freely because nothing depends on it\").\n21\t\n22\t- **MUST** / **MUST NOT** — an absolute requirement; an implementation violating it does not conform to this spec, and no fragment, deployment, or phase may relax it.\n23\t- **SHOULD** / **SHOULD NOT** — recommended; deviation is permitted only with a documented rationale (this plan's `acknowledged`-valued fields — `x-unscrubbable`, `insecureSkipVerify`, `x-upstream-plaintext` — are its concrete, enumerable form).\n24\t- **MAY** — truly optional, of no consequence to conformance either way.\n25\t\n26\t## Overview\n27\t\n28\tSEAM (Self-documenting Endpoint Access Mediator) is a single unified endpoint that acts as a proxy to multiple authenticated services. It injects the required secret into a request received from an agent, sends the request on to the destination service, and passes the response back — the agent never sees the secret. It also self-documents: a merged OpenAPI spec drives `/docs` and `/openapi.json`, and malformed requests get a structured error naming the bad field and pointing at the right shape, instead of a bare 400.\n29\t\n30\t## Motivation\n31\t\n32\tToday, each backend service (ArgoCD read-only proxy, per-cluster kubectl-proxy, the z.ai/GLM proxy, the twitterapi.io proxy) is documented by hand in CLAUDE.md with its own discovery and auth pattern. This doesn't scale: every new service needs new hand-written prose, agents have no standard way to discover what's available, and there's no mechanism to guide an agent that sends a malformed request back toward the correct one.\n33\t\n34\t## Glossary\n35\t\n36\tThe load-bearing coined terms of this plan, defined once so fragment authors — who are largely agents, and often several of them working the same tree — share one vocabulary (added 2026-07-21; a framing artifact, not a new decision — every definition is mined from the section that owns the term).\n37\t\n38\t- **fragment** — a per-service OpenAPI 3.1 paths/components fragment plus SEAM extension fields (`x-upstream`, `x-vault-path`, `x-inject-as`, …), delivered as one Kubernetes ConfigMap per upstream service and mounted at `/etc/gateway/routes.d/<svc>/`. The unit of route authoring, versioning, and retirement; a service ships N of them under one owner directory.\n39\t- **route fragment schema / `x-seam-schema`** — the JSON Schema a fragment must satisfy (`x-seam-schema: v1`, a fragment-root marker). `x-seam-schema` versions the fragment *format SEAM parses*; it is distinct from `x-api-version`, which versions the *contract SEAM serves to callers*.\n40\t- **owner chain** — the forgery-resistant binding `k8s/rs-manager/seam/routes/<svc>/` → ConfigMap `seam-routes-<svc>` → `mountPath /etc/gateway/routes.d/<svc>/` → `x-seam-owner: <svc>` → `x-vault-path ⊂ seam/routes/<svc>/*`. Its first three links are operator-owned (in SEAM's own manifest, not writable by a fragment author); `seam lint` is the only consumer that walks it whole, the gateway re-checks the last three at runtime from what it can observe.\n41\t- **co-ownership rule** — a fragment's `x-vault-path` may reference only `seam/routes/<x-seam-owner>/*`, so \"point service A's secret at service B's upstream\" fails on ownership even inside the vault-path allowlist.\n42\t- **upstream-host allowlist** vs **vault-path allowlist** — the two peer anti-exfiltration controls. The vault-path allowlist bounds *which secret* a fragment may name (the `seam/routes/*` prefix + co-ownership); the upstream-host allowlist (`seam-upstream-allowlist`) bounds *where that secret is sent* (permitted host suffixes and enumerated bare hostnames). Both operator-owned, both in SEAM's manifest and never in a fragment, both enforced twice (lint + merge-time quarantine).\n43\t- **adapter / `x-adapter`** — a declarative, closed-vocabulary request/response transform carried by an *older* coexisting fragment, converting its contract into the newest version's so SEAM needs no N parallel implementations. Data, not code — so a contract migration is a ConfigMap edit, never a gateway binary deploy.\n44\t- **quiet window** — the retirement drain period: how long a route-version's request counter must read zero before it may retire. Traffic-adaptive with a 7-day calendar floor, `max(3 × observed max inter-request gap, 7 days)`, read from the metrics store (Phase 8).\n45\t- **brownout** — scheduled final-week `410 Gone` windows served on a deprecated route-version, converting \"we believe nobody calls this\" into a tested claim an LLM caller can read and self-migrate from. A caller appearing during one **cancels** retirement rather than being sacrificed to it.\n46\t- **retirement** — usage-gated removal of a drained fragment, via an operator-merged declarative-config PR opened by `seam-retirement-evaluator`. Zero observed traffic is a necessary condition; a date never triggers it.\n47\t- **`_all`** — the reserved instance-selector value that fans a request out to every mapped `x-upstream-map` instance concurrently and returns one instance-labeled merged envelope; invoking it requires the fragment-root `x-fanout-scope`.\n48\t- **`_unversioned`** — the reserved `x-api-version` key for fragments predating versioning. Sorts strictly oldest, so it stays the default for callers sending no `X-SEAM-API-Version`; assigned by SEAM, a lint error if *authored*, but a legal value to *address*.\n49\t- **`x-instance-param`** — the fragment-root field naming which path parameter selects an `x-upstream-map` entry (e.g. `cluster` for `/k8s/{cluster}/…`). `{instance}` throughout this plan is its generic stand-in; a real fragment names it concretely.\n50\t- **scope-withheld** — a fan-out envelope status for an instance dropped from `_all` because the caller lacks its per-instance `requiredScope`: nothing dispatched, no `httpStatus`, no body, charged nothing — distinguishable from `error`, `timeout` and `breaker-refused`.\n51\t- **breaker-refused** — a fan-out envelope status for an instance whose circuit breaker was open: not dispatched, no secret read, charged nothing, carrying the breaker's `openedAt`/`lastError`/`retryAfter` so it is diagnosable without a second call.\n52\t- **tumbling window** — a guard/quota window anchored at process start (`^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d)$`, no calendar-aligned form): it opens at start, closes `window` later, the next opens immediately with the counter cleared, and a SEAM restart resets it unconditionally.\n53\t- **pass-through fragment** — a route declaring neither `x-vault-path` nor `x-inject-as` (both-or-neither): SEAM forwards it with TLS, guards, health and versioning intact but injects nothing, scrubbing is a no-op, and it contributes no `/health/credentials` entry. The Phase 3 ArgoCD pilot is one.\n54\t- **the pipeline** — the fixed **11-stage inbound / 4-stage outbound** request path (Architecture). \"Stage N\" everywhere in this plan means a position in those two lists and no other count is normative; the stages MUST NOT be reordered.\n55\t- **control-plane surface** vs **caller-facing surface** — the control-plane surface is SEAM's own endpoints, resolved at pipeline stage 1 before the merged route table, in two tiers: caller-facing-and-scope-filtered (`/openapi.json`, `/docs`, `/docs/route`, `/whoami`, `/scopes`, `/changes`) and operator-only default-denied (`/config/status`, `/health/credentials`, `/health/upstreams`, behind `seam:ops:read`). The caller-facing surface is the proxy front door agents call, bound to the caller-facing listener port `8080` (the operator tier binds `8081`); SEAM's own base URL — the caller port's external address — populates the merged spec's `servers:`.\n56\t- **spec version (`X-SEAM-Spec-Version`)** vs **API version (`x-api-version`)** — the two distinct version spaces, both spellable on a `?version=` parameter but never on the same endpoint. `X-SEAM-Spec-Version` is a hash of the whole currently-served merged spec (the archive key on `/openapi.json?version=`); `x-api-version` is a per-route contract marker, `v<n>` or `_unversioned` (the selector on `/docs/route?version=`). A value from the wrong alphabet is a 400 naming which the endpoint expects.\n57\t- **Grant / WhoIs** — Tailscale identity terms. A caller's scope claims (`service:action`, e.g. `k8s-ro:get`) travel in the Tailscale **Grant**'s `app` capability field, read via **`WhoIs`** on the inbound connection — the tailnet-native authorization source Phase 7 enforces `x-required-scope` against.\n58\t- **fan-out envelope** — the single buffered JSON object an `_all` request returns: `{instances, summary}`, keyed by instance, scrubbed exactly once against the union of every injected value, and bounded by `maxFanoutEnvelopeBytes` (overflowing instances become `truncated`).\n59\t- **sentinel probe** — a byte-identical authenticated request the credential sentinel issues per fragment on its `x-credential-probe` cadence to validate a credential against its upstream. Carries an unforgeable in-process origin tag; excluded from the retirement, loop-breaker and quota counters, but counted — deliberately — in last-2xx and breaker state.\n60\t\n61\t## Non-Goals and What SEAM Is Not\n62\t\n63\tEvery boundary below is traceable to a decision already in this plan; this section consolidates them so scope creep is caught by reference rather than re-argued (added 2026-07-21).\n64\t\n65\t**Non-Goals (v1):**\n66\t\n67\t- **Not highly available / multi-replica** — because guard counters, quota ledgers, last-2xx and breaker state are per-process and in-memory by design, and a second replica behind one Service silently doubles every threshold (a loop guard of 10 permits 20, a `$50` `x-quota` permits `$100`). Single-replica (`replicas: 1`, `maxSurge: 0`) is a load-bearing invariant; HA is a documented later upgrade path — a shared state store for counters/ledgers/breaker plus leader election for the sentinel (Version Migration Strategy §1) — not a v1 deliverable, and never reachable by raising `replicas`.\n68\t- **Not an accounting system of record** — because `x-quota` is a runaway-spend *brake*: its windows are tumbling and restart-scoped, so a binary deploy resets every budget, and `X-SEAM-Budget-Remaining` is a fleet-wide fuel gauge, not a reservation (Per-Route Guards). The durable substrate for anything that must survive a restart is the metrics store (VictoriaMetrics), which is where retirement reads its evidence — SEAM's own memory is not.\n69\t- **Not a general-purpose API gateway or WAF** — because SEAM fronts a fixed, operator-curated set of fleet upstreams bounded by the upstream-host allowlist, not arbitrary traffic. There is no rate-limiting-as-a-service, no request transformation beyond the closed `x-adapter` version vocabulary, and no destination an operator has not enumerated in SEAM's own manifest.\n70\t- **Not a secrets manager** — because OpenBao remains the store of record; SEAM authenticates via Kubernetes auth and reads a single bounded prefix (`seam/routes/*`) at request time, holding secrets only in a 30-second in-memory cache (Architecture). It stores nothing, rotates nothing, and issues nothing.\n71\t- **Not a public-internet ingress in v1** — because SEAM is reachable only behind the tag-restricted tailnet ACL until Phase 7 (Pre-Phase-7 Trust Boundary); no Funnel, no public ingress, no Cloudflare Tunnel before then. The non-tailnet (foreign-worker) bearer path is Phase 14, and it is the *only* phase that lifts this rule.\n72\t- **Not a replacement for ArgoCD or GitOps** — because fragments ship through `jedarden/declarative-config` and are synced by ArgoCD like every other cluster change (CLAUDE.md); SEAM adds a hot-reload path *within* an onboarded service, it does not bypass the GitOps repo. Retirement itself is a declarative-config PR a human merges.\n73\t- **Not client-side tool restriction** — because scope enforcement is server-side and default-deny (`x-required-scope`, Grant-checked at pipeline stage 5). Never rely on the calling agent's own tool list as the boundary — client-side restriction is UX, not security (Per-Agent Tool Scoping point 3).\n74\t\n75\t**What SEAM Is Not** (the plan's scattered is-not statements, consolidated):\n76\t\n77\t- **Not stateless** — emphatically. It holds per-process, load-bearing state (guard counters, quota ledgers, last-2xx, breaker state, the sentinel's probe loop), which is exactly why it runs single-replica (Version Migration Strategy §1).\n78\t- **Not a proxy that trusts caller headers** — it is strip-then-inject, never trust-then-overlay: every injectable header *and* injected query-parameter name, plus `Authorization` and all `X-SEAM-*` request headers bar the documented exceptions, are deleted on ingress before injection (Architecture, pipeline stage 2).\n79\t- **Not an open proxy** — the dual operator-owned allowlists (vault-path and upstream-host) plus default-deny at every boundary mean a correctly-filed, correctly-owned fragment still cannot name an arbitrary secret or an arbitrary destination (Architecture; Pre-Phase-7 Trust Boundary).\n80\t- **Not calendar-gated on retirement** — zero observed traffic is a *necessary* condition; a calendar term (the 7-day floor) may only ever lengthen the wait, never trigger a removal on its own (Version Migration Strategy §2; Phase 8).\n81\t- **Not a place where a fragment author self-certifies** — the owner chain and both allowlists live in SEAM's own manifest (`k8s/rs-manager/seam/`), outside every `routes/<svc>/` directory, so the author who would name a malicious host or secret cannot also write the rule that permits it (Architecture; Components).\n82\t\n83\t## Acceptance Scenarios\n84\t\n85\tThese nine named scenarios are the independently-verifiable definitions of \"correct\" a build is checked against, each written as **Setup → Action → Expected → Pass criteria → Fail criteria**; they are the external oracle the Testing Strategy's acceptance suite implements (see **Testing Strategy** below), and every criterion here is traceable to a behavior specified elsewhere in this plan rather than introduced with it (added 2026-07-21). They are worded to be checkable by a test harness that observes SEAM's inbound response, its upstream request, and its control-plane surfaces — never SEAM's internal state — because that is exactly the boundary an agent sees. Where a scenario's behavior changes at Phase 7 (identity) or Phase 8 (versioning), the phase-conditioned form is stated, since a build is checked against the behavior of the phase it claims to have shipped.\n86\t\n87\t### Scenario 1: Secret injection and echo-scrubbing (happy path)\n88\t\n89\t**Setup.** A single-instance proxied route declaring `x-vault-path` (inside `seam/routes/<x-seam-owner>/*`) and `x-inject-as` `{kind, name}` — e.g. a Phase 4 z.ai/GLM or twitterapi.io fragment — whose upstream is reachable and whose OpenBao secret exists. The caller sends its own copy of the injected header or query-parameter name, its own `Authorization`, and several `X-SEAM-*` request headers, and the upstream is one that echoes the presented credential back in an error body.\n90\t\n91\t**Action.** The caller invokes the route.\n92\t\n93\t**Expected.** Pipeline stage 2 strips every injectable header, every occurrence of the injected query-parameter name, `Authorization`, and all `X-SEAM-*` request headers bar the two documented caller-supplied exceptions; stage 10 resolves the secret (30s cache or OpenBao) and injects exactly one credential per `x-inject-as`; stage 11 forwards; outbound stage 4 scrubs the exact injected value(s) out of the response body, headers and trailers, redacting to `[REDACTED-BY-SEAM]`.\n94\t\n95\t**Pass criteria.**\n96\t- The injected value appears in **no** returned byte — body, headers, or trailers — including the upstream error body that echoes it, which arrives at the caller with the value replaced by `[REDACTED-BY-SEAM]`.\n97\t- The upstream request carries **exactly one** injected credential under the declared `x-inject-as.name` (or `Authorization: Bearer <secret>` for `kind: bearer`), and it is SEAM's fetched value, not the caller's copy.\n98\t- The caller's `Authorization`, every `X-SEAM-*` request header except `X-SEAM-Dry-Run` and `X-SEAM-API-Version`, and every caller-supplied instance of the injected header/query name (all occurrences; case-insensitive per-key for headers, exact for query keys) are **absent** from the upstream request.\n99\t\n100\t**Fail criteria.**"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":"call_5d6840d6288a4469b45e15f8","session_id":"38f71f27-e6fe-4d23-9b52-7faf2f6c093e","uuid":"42c60af1-c2aa-432e-bfcd-b0538bed4d98","timestamp":"2026-07-27T16:25:17.927Z","subagent_type":"Explore","task_description":"Explore argocd-ro proxy code"}

Base64-encoded request/response bodies\n  - Canonicalized HTTP headers\n  - Auto-save every 10 entries to prevent data loss\n  - Graceful shutdown with corpus persistence\n\n#### 2. **Corpus Format** (`seam-diff-corpus/v1` schema)\n```json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:02:06-04:00\",\n  \"entries\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"api-v1-applications-get\",\n      \"request\": {\n        \"method\": \"GET\",\n        \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n        \"headers\": {\"Accept\": [\"*/*\"]},\n        \"bodyB64\": \"\"\n      },\n      \"secrets\": [\n        {\n          \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n          \"injectAs\": {\"kind\": \"bearer\"}\n        }\n      ]\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n#### 3. **Control Scripts** (`/home/coding/SEAM/scripts/capture-argocd.sh`)\n- `start` - Launch capture proxy on port 8082\n- `stop` - Gracefully stop and save corpus  \n- `status` - Show capture status and entry count\n- Configurable via environment variables\n\n#### 4. **Security Model**\n- **Credentials stored as references only** (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n- Never literal values in corpus files\n- Git-tracked corpus files are safe to commit\n- Literal values resolved at replay-time from local secrets source\n\n## 3. Existing ArgoCD Corpus Data\n\n### Current Corpus (`/home/coding/SEAM/corpus/argocd-proxy/corpus.json`)\nCurrently contains **2 captured entries**:\n1. `api-v1-applications-get` - List all applications\n2. `api-v1-clusters-get` - List all clusters\n\n### Corpus Template (`corpus-template.json`)\nDefines the complete expected ArgoCD API coverage:\n- `GET /api/v1/applications` - List all applications\n- `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}` - Get specific application\n- `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` - Get sync status\n- `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/manifest` - Get application manifest\n- `GET /api/v1/clusters` - List all clusters\n\n## 4. Differential Testing Infrastructure\n\n### seam-replay Tool (`/home/coding/SEAM/tools/diffharness/cmd/seam-replay/main.go`)\nReplays captured corpus against both incumbent and SEAM implementations:\n\n```\nseam-replay → Incumbent Proxy → Response (baseline)\n              │\n              └─→ SEAM Gateway → Response (compared to baseline)\n```\n\n### Comparison Engine (`/home/coding/SEAM/tools/diffharness/internal/compare/compare.go`)\n- **Security-first approach**: Secret leak detection runs first and independently\n- **Response equivalence testing**: Status codes, headers, bodies after secret redaction\n- **Expected diffs handling**: X-SEAM-* headers, volatile headers (Date, Server)\n- **Verdict system**: PASS/FAIL/SKIP with detailed reasons\n\n### Secret Resolution (`/home/coding/SEAM/tools/diffharness/internal/secref/secref.go`)\n- Two-layer resolution: JSON file → environment variables\n- Environment variable pattern: `SEAM_DIFF_SECRET_vault_seam_routes_argocd_ro_token`\n- Only place in the system that holds literal secret values (in-memory only)\n\n## 5. The corpus serves as the oracle for differential testing during service migration to SEAM.\n\n## Design Principles\n\n1. **Security-First:** Credentials stored as references only, never literal values\n2. **Git-Tracked:** Corpus files are committed to version control for reproducibility\n3. **Replayable:** Each entry can be replayed verbatim against both incumbent and SEAM\n4. **Differential-Ready:** Structured for comparison between two HTTP responses\n5. **Self-Documenting:** Human-readable descriptions and stable IDs\n\n## JSON Schema Definition\n\n### Top-Level Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"description\": \"ArgoCD read-only proxy corpus captured from production\",\n  \"entries\": []\n}\n```\n\n### Field Definitions\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `schema` | string | Yes | Schema version identifier. Must be `\"seam-diff-corpus/v1\"` |\n| `service` | string | Yes | Service name token. Must be `\"argocd\"` |\n| `incumbent` | string | Yes | Base URL of incumbent proxy captured against |\n| `capturedAt` | string | Yes | RFC3339 timestamp of first capture |\n| `description` | string | Yes | Free-form description of the corpus |\n| `entries` | array | Yes | Array of corpus entry objects |\n\n### Entry Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"list-applications-get\",\n  \"description\": \"List all ArgoCD applications\",\n  \"request\": {\n    \"method\": \"GET\",\n    \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n    \"query\": \"\",\n    \"headers\": {\n      \"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]\n    },\n    \"bodyB64\": \"\",\n    \"bodyContentType\": \"\"\n  },\n  \"secrets\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n      \"injectAs\": {\n        \"kind\": \"bearer\"\n      }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"expect\": {\n    \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\"]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Entry Field Definitions\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `id` | string | Yes | Stable, human-readable entry ID (kebab-case) |\n| `description` | string | No | What this entry exercises |\n| `request` | object | Yes | HTTP request object (see below) |\n| `secrets` | array | No | Secret reference objects |\n| `expect` | object | No | Per-entry comparison overrides |\n\n### Request Object Schema\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `method` | string | Yes | HTTP method (canonicalized: GET, POST, etc.) |\n| `path` | string | Yes | Request path only, no query string |\n| `query` | string | No | Query string without leading `?` |\n| `headers` | object | No | Header map with canonicalized keys |\n| `bodyB64` | string | No | Base64-encoded request body |\n| `bodyContentType` | string | No | Content-Type of request body |\n\n### Secret Reference Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n  \"injectAs\": {\n    \"kind\": \"bearer\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `ref` | string | Yes | Secret reference path (e.g., `vault:...`) |\n| `injectAs` | object | Yes | Injection specification (see below) |\n\n### InjectAs Schema\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `kind` | string | Yes | Injection method: `header`, `bearer`, or `query` |\n| `name` | string | Conditional | Header/query name (required for `header`/`query`, rejected for `bearer`) |\n\n### Expect Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": 200,\n  \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\", \"X-Request-Id\"],\n  \"ignoreBody\": false,\n  \"skip\": \"\"\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `status` | int | No | Expected status code (nil means differential comparison) |\n| `ignoreHeaders` | array | No | Header names to ignore during comparison |\n| `ignoreBody` | bool | No | Skip body comparison entirely |\n| `skip` | string | No | Skip reason (empty = not skipped) |\n\n## File Organization Structure\n\n### Directory Layout\n\n```\ncorpus/\n├── README.md                           # Corpus capture documentation\n├── capture-config.yaml                 # Global capture configuration\n└── argocd-proxy/\n    ├── README.md                       # ArgoCD-specific documentation\n    ├── corpus.json                     # Primary corpus file\n    ├── corpus-template.json            # Template with example entries\n    ├── applications-list.json          # Per-endpoint capture files (optional)\n    ├── clusters-list.json              # Per-endpoint capture files (optional)\n    └── metadata/\n        ├── capture-session.json        # Session metadata\n        └── validation-report.json      # Validation results\n```\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**Primary corpus file:** `corpus.json`\n- Single source of truth for differential testing\n- Sorted by entry ID for stable diffs\n- Git-tracked\n\n**Per-endpoint captures:** `{endpoint}-{method}.json`\n- Optional granular capture files\n- Useful for debugging specific endpoints\n- Merged into primary corpus before testing\n\n**Template file:** `corpus-template.json`\n- Example entries showing all fields\n- Reference for manual corpus creation\n- Not used in automated testing\n\n## Metadata Format\n\n### Timestamps\n\n**Format:** RFC3339 with timezone offset\n\n**Locations:**\n1. **Corpus-level:** `capturedAt` field\n   - Set on first capture\n   - Never updated on subsequent appends\n   - Example: `\"2026-07-27T12:00:00-04:00\"`\n\n2. **Entry-level:** (optional) `capturedAt` in entry metadata\n   - Capture time of individual entry\n   - Useful for chronological analysis\n   - Not required for replay\n\n### Request IDs\n\n**Entry ID generation:**\n\n```\nentryID(path, method) = kebab-case(path) + \"-\" + lower(method)\n```\n\n**Examples:**\n- `/api/v1/applications` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-get`\n- `/api/v1/clusters/{name}` + `GET` → `api-v1-clusters-name-get`\n- `/api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-name-sync-get`\n\n**Manual IDs:** For special cases, IDs can be manually specified:\n- `health-check-get`\n- `metrics-get`\n- `streaming-logs-post`\n\n### Session Metadata\n\n**File:** `corpus/argocd-proxy/metadata/capture-session.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"sessionId\": \"capture-2026-07-27-120000\",\n  \"startedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00-04:00\",\n  \"endedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:15:30-04:00\",\n  \"captureTool\": \"seam-capture\",\n  \"captureToolVersion\": \"v0.1.0\",\n  \"incumbentUrl\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"entriesCaptured\": 15,\n  \"captureDurationSeconds\": 930,\n  \"captureHost\": \"localhost\",\n  \"capturePort\": 8082\n}\n```\n\n## ArgoCD-Specific Considerations\n\n### Key API Endpoints\n\n**Applications:**\n1. `GET /api/v1/applications` - List all applications\n2. `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}` - Get specific application\n3. `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` - Get sync status\n4. `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}/manifest` - Get application manifest\n\n**Clusters:**\n1. `GET /api/v1/clusters` - List all clusters\n2. `GET /api/v1/clusters/{name}` - Get specific cluster details\n\n**Repositories:**\n1. `GET /api/v1/repositories` - List repositories\n2. `GET /api/v1/repositories/{url}` - Get specific repository\n\n### Headers to Always Ignore\n\nArgoCD API returns volatile headers that should always be ignored:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"expect\": {\n    \"ignoreHeaders\": [\n      \"Date\",\n      \"Server\",\n      \"X-Request-Id\",\n      \"Set-Cookie\",\n      \"ETag\"\n    ]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Secret Injection Pattern\n\nAll ArgoCD API requests require bearer authentication:\n\n```json\n{\n  \"secrets\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n      \"injectAs\": {\n        \"kind\": \"bearer\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n## Security Considerations\n\n### Credential Safety\n\n✅ **Safe:**\n- Secret references (e.g., `vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token`)\n- Git-tracked corpus files\n- Shared in pull requests\n\n❌ **Never:**\n- Literal credential values in corpus files\n- Base64-encoded credentials (except request/response bodies)\n- Personal access tokens or API keys\n\n### Corpus Review Checklist\n\nBefore The corpus serves as the oracle for differential testing during service migration to SEAM.\n\n## Design Principles\n\n1. **Security-First:** Credentials stored as references only, never literal values\n2. **Git-Tracked:** Corpus files are committed to version control for reproducibility\n3. **Replayable:** Each entry can be replayed verbatim against both incumbent and SEAM\n4. **Differential-Ready:** Structured for comparison between two HTTP responses\n5. **Self-Documenting:** Human-readable descriptions and stable IDs\n\n## JSON Schema Definition\n\n### Top-Level Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"schema\": \"seam-diff-corpus/v1\",\n  \"service\": \"argocd\",\n  \"incumbent\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"capturedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00Z\",\n  \"description\": \"ArgoCD read-only proxy corpus captured from production\",\n  \"entries\": []\n}\n```\n\n### Field Definitions\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `schema` | string | Yes | Schema version identifier. Must be `\"seam-diff-corpus/v1\"` |\n| `service` | string | Yes | Service name token. Must be `\"argocd\"` |\n| `incumbent` | string | Yes | Base URL of incumbent proxy captured against |\n| `capturedAt` | string | Yes | RFC3339 timestamp of first capture |\n| `description` | string | Yes | Free-form description of the corpus |\n| `entries` | array | Yes | Array of corpus entry objects |\n\n### Entry Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"id\": \"list-applications-get\",\n  \"description\": \"List all ArgoCD applications\",\n  \"request\": {\n    \"method\": \"GET\",\n    \"path\": \"/api/v1/applications\",\n    \"query\": \"\",\n    \"headers\": {\n      \"Accept\": [\"application/json\"]\n    },\n    \"bodyB64\": \"\",\n    \"bodyContentType\": \"\"\n  },\n  \"secrets\": [\n    {\n      \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n      \"injectAs\": {\n        \"kind\": \"bearer\"\n      }\n    }\n  ],\n  \"expect\": {\n    \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\"]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n### Entry Field Definitions\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `id` | string | Yes | Stable, human-readable entry ID (kebab-case) |\n| `description` | string | No | What this entry exercises |\n| `request` | object | Yes | HTTP request object (see below) |\n| `secrets` | array | No | Secret reference objects |\n| `expect` | object | No | Per-entry comparison overrides |\n\n### Request Object Schema\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `method` | string | Yes | HTTP method (canonicalized: GET, POST, etc.) |\n| `path` | string | Yes | Request path only, no query string |\n| `query` | string | No | Query string without leading `?` |\n| `headers` | object | No | Header map with canonicalized keys |\n| `bodyB64` | string | No | Base64-encoded request body |\n| `bodyContentType` | string | No | Content-Type of request body |\n\n### Secret Reference Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"ref\": \"vault:seam/routes/argocd/ro-token\",\n  \"injectAs\": {\n    \"kind\": \"bearer\"\n  }\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `ref` | string | Yes | Secret reference path (e.g., `vault:...`) |\n| `injectAs` | object | Yes | Injection specification (see below) |\n\n### InjectAs Schema\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `kind` | string | Yes | Injection method: `header`, `bearer`, or `query` |\n| `name` | string | Conditional | Header/query name (required for `header`/`query`, rejected for `bearer`) |\n\n### Expect Schema\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": 200,\n  \"ignoreHeaders\": [\"Date\", \"Server\", \"X-Request-Id\"],\n  \"ignoreBody\": false,\n  \"skip\": \"\"\n}\n```\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `status` | int | No | Expected status code (nil means differential comparison) |\n| `ignoreHeaders` | array | No | Header names to ignore during comparison |\n| `ignoreBody` | bool | No | Skip body comparison entirely |\n| `skip` | string | No | Skip reason (empty = not skipped) |\n\n## File Organization Structure\n\n### Directory Layout\n\n```\ncorpus/\n├── README.md                           # Corpus capture documentation\n├── capture-config.yaml                 # Global capture configuration\n└── argocd-proxy/\n    ├── README.md                       # ArgoCD-specific documentation\n    ├── corpus.json                     # Primary corpus file\n    ├── corpus-template.json            # Template with example entries\n    ├── applications-list.json          # Per-endpoint capture files (optional)\n    ├── clusters-list.json              # Per-endpoint capture files (optional)\n    └── metadata/\n        ├── capture-session.json        # Session metadata\n        └── validation-report.json      # Validation results\n```\n\n### File Naming Conventions\n\n**Primary corpus file:** `corpus.json`\n- Single source of truth for differential testing\n- Sorted by entry ID for stable diffs\n- Git-tracked\n\n**Per-endpoint captures:** `{endpoint}-{method}.json`\n- Optional granular capture files\n- Useful for debugging specific endpoints\n- Merged into primary corpus before testing\n\n**Template file:** `corpus-template.json`\n- Example entries showing all fields\n- Reference for manual corpus creation\n- Not used in automated testing\n\n## Metadata Format\n\n### Timestamps\n\n**Format:** RFC3339 with timezone offset\n\n**Locations:**\n1. **Corpus-level:** `capturedAt` field\n   - Set on first capture\n   - Never updated on subsequent appends\n   - Example: `\"2026-07-27T12:00:00-04:00\"`\n\n2. **Entry-level:** (optional) `capturedAt` in entry metadata\n   - Capture time of individual entry\n   - Useful for chronological analysis\n   - Not required for replay\n\n### Request IDs\n\n**Entry ID generation:**\n\n```\nentryID(path, method) = kebab-case(path) + \"-\" + lower(method)\n```\n\n**Examples:**\n- `/api/v1/applications` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-get`\n- `/api/v1/clusters/{name}` + `GET` → `api-v1-clusters-name-get`\n- `/api/v1/applications/{name}/sync` + `GET` → `api-v1-applications-name-sync-get`\n\n**Manual IDs:** For special cases, IDs can be manually specified:\n- `health-check-get`\n- `metrics-get`\n- `streaming-logs-post`\n\n### Session Metadata\n\n**File:** `corpus/argocd-proxy/metadata/capture-session.json`\n\n```json\n{\n  \"sessionId\": \"capture-2026-07-27-120000\",\n  \"startedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:00:00-04:00\",\n  \"endedAt\": \"2026-07-27T12:15:30-04:00\",\n  \"captureTool\": \"seam-capture\",\n  \"captureToolVersion\": \"v0.1.0\",\n  \"incumbentUrl\": \"https://argocd-ro-ardenone-manager-ts.ardenone.com:8444\",\n  \"entriesCaptured\": 15,\n  \"captureDurationSeconds\": 930,\n  \"captureHost\": \"localhost\",\n  \"capturePort\": 8082\n}\n```\n\n## ArgoCD-Specific Considerations\n\n### Key API Endpoints\n\n**Applications:**\n1. `GET /api/v1/applications` - List all applications\n2. `GET /api/v1/applications/{name}` - Get specific application\n3.
